bibl.title: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Statement

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: What an accurate and complete report of a cohort, case-control or cross-sectional study must contain.
span.quote: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Initiative developed recommendations on what should be included in an accurate and complete report of an observational study.

span.label: Observational research is often reported so incompletely that a reader cannot judge it - what minimum set of items would fix that?
span.quote: Much biomedical research is observational. The reporting of such research is often inadequate, which hampers the assessment of its strengths and weaknesses and of a study's generalisability.

span.label: A 22-item checklist, 18 items shared across three observational designs and four design-specific, arrived at by workshop and iterative consultation.
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: method
span.quote: The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Initiative developed recommendations on what should be included in an accurate and complete report of an observational study.

span.label: reporting quality of observational epidemiological studies
span.quote: The reporting of such research is often inadequate, which hampers the assessment of its strengths and weaknesses and of a study's generalisability.

span.label: consensus-guideline-development
span.quote: We convened a 2-day workshop in September 2004, with methodologists, researchers, and journal editors to draft a checklist of items.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a reader can only assess a study from what is written down, so completeness of the report is the precondition for any critical assessment at all
span.quote: The credibility of research depends on a critical assessment by others of the strengths and weaknesses in study design, conduct, and analysis.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the precedent is that a checklist actually works: CONSORT measurably improved the reporting of randomised trials
span.quote: Many medical journals supported this initiative [ 13 ], which has helped to improve the quality of reports of randomised trials [ 14 , 15 ].

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: adoption runs through journals rather than authors - editorial staff of seven journals sat in the room where the list was drafted
span.quote: 23 individuals attended this meeting, including editorial staff from Annals of Internal Medicine , BMJ , Bulletin of the World Health Organization , International Journal of Epidemiology , JAMA , Preventive Medicine , and The Lancet, as well as epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, and practitioners from Europe and North America.

span.label: in published observational research important information is often missing or unclear (the gap STROBE addresses)
span.quote: in published observational research important information is often missing or unclear

span.label: STROBE covers only three observational designs and does not yet extend to others such as case-crossover or ecological studies.
span.quote: We acknowledge that STROBE is currently limited to three main observational study designs.

span.label: No comprehensive systematic review was done for the individual checklist items and no new research was conducted to fill evidence gaps.
span.quote: We did not undertake a comprehensive systematic review for each of the checklist items and sub-items, or do our own research to fill gaps in the evidence base.

span.label: The group of contributors was shaped by existing networks and was not geographically or disciplinarily representative.
span.quote: Further, although no one was excluded from the process, the composition of the group of contributors was influenced by existing networks and was not representative in terms of geography (it was dominated by contributors from Europe and North America) and probably was not representative in terms of research interests and disciplines.

span.label: The checklist is explicitly not a quality-assessment instrument for observational research.
span.quote: We emphasise that the STROBE Statement was not developed as a tool for assessing the quality of published observational research.

span.label: Covers only three observational designs; case-crossover and ecological studies are outside it.
span.quote: We acknowledge that STROBE is currently limited to three main observational study designs.

span.label: The authors explicitly disclaim rigidity and standardisation - the items must be addressed somewhere, in any order or format.
span.quote: The STROBE Statement should not be interpreted as an attempt to prescribe the reporting of observational research in a rigid format.

span.label: The checklist is not a quality-assessment instrument, and the paper says so to forestall exactly that use.
span.quote: Also, while clarity of reporting is a prerequisite to evaluation, the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.

span.label: the epidemiological and statistical methodology of observational study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) and confounding control, standardized for transparent medical reporting
span.quote: We defined the scope of the recommendations to cover three main study designs: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies

span.label: STROBE
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: checklist
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: observational studies
span.quote: We decided to focus on the 3 study designs that are used most widely in analytical observational research: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies.

span.label: randomised trials
span.quote: Randomised trials cannot answer all important questions about a given intervention.

span.label: CONSORT
span.quote: The Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) Statement was developed in 1996 and revised 5 years later [ 12 ].

span.label: STREGA
span.quote: A first extension to STROBE is underway for gene-disease association studies: the STROBE Extension to Genetic Association studies (STREGA) initiative [ 25 ].

span.label: transparent reporting
span.quote: Research should be reported transparently so that readers can follow what was planned, what was done, what was found, and what conclusions were drawn.

span.label: instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research
span.term: instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research
span.quote: Also, while clarity of reporting is a prerequisite to evaluation, the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.

span.label: prescriptions for designing or conducting studies
span.term: prescriptions for designing or conducting studies
span.quote: The intention is solely to provide guidance on how to report observational research well: these recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies.

span.label: confounding variables
span.quote: An analysis of epidemiological studies published in general medical and specialist journals found that the rationale behind the choice of potential confounding variables was often not reported [ 6 ].

span.label: quality - of the REPORT: whether a reader can follow what was planned, done and found. This is what STROBE addresses
span.quote: Research should be reported transparently so that readers can follow what was planned, what was done, what was found, and what conclusions were drawn.

span.label: quality - of the RESEARCH itself: how good the study is. The paper states explicitly that the checklist does not measure this
span.quote: Also, while clarity of reporting is a prerequisite to evaluation, the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.

span.label: guidance - on how to WRITE UP a study, as opposed to guidance on how to design or conduct one
span.quote: The intention is solely to provide guidance on how to report observational research well: these recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies.

span.label: builds-on → the CONSORT Statement for reporting randomised trials
span.quote: We developed the checklist through an open process, taking into account the experience gained with previous initiatives, in particular CONSORT.

span.label: builds-on → the CONSORT Statement for randomised trials [ 12 ]
span.quote: The Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) Statement was developed in 1996 and revised 5 years later [ 12 ].

span.label: extends → empirical surveys of reporting deficiencies in epidemiology, psychiatry and stroke research
span.quote: In a survey of longitudinal studies in stroke research, 17 of 49 articles (35%) did not specify the eligibility criteria [ 8 ].

span.label: STROBE —is-a→ checklist
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: STROBE —distinct-from→ instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research
span.term: instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research
span.quote: Also, while clarity of reporting is a prerequisite to evaluation, the checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.

span.label: STROBE —distinct-from→ prescriptions for designing or conducting studies
span.term: prescriptions for designing or conducting studies
span.quote: The intention is solely to provide guidance on how to report observational research well: these recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies.

span.label: STREGA —part-of→ STROBE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the paper says 'extension to STROBE'. An extension is a derivative rather than a component; part-of is the nearest of the eight and the fit is loose.
span.quote: A first extension to STROBE is underway for gene-disease association studies: the STROBE Extension to Genetic Association studies (STREGA) initiative [ 25 ].

span.label: observational studies —contrasted-with→ randomised trials
span.quote: observational studies are more suitable to detect rare or late adverse effects of treatments, and are more likely to provide an indication of what is achieved in daily medical practice [ 3 ]

span.label: 22 — number of checklist items in the STROBE Statement
span.quote: resulted in a checklist of 22 items (the STROBE Statement)

span.label: three — designs covered: cohort, case-control, cross-sectional
span.quote: to cover three main study designs: cohort, case-control

span.label: 22 items — size of the checklist
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: 18 common, 4 design-specific — how the checklist splits across the three designs
span.quote: 18 items are common to all three study designs and four are specific for cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional studies.

span.label: 17 of 49 articles (35%) — longitudinal stroke studies that did not specify eligibility criteria
span.quote: In a survey of longitudinal studies in stroke research, 17 of 49 articles (35%) did not specify the eligibility criteria [ 8 ].

span.label: 23 individuals — attendance at the workshop that drafted the checklist
span.quote: 23 individuals attended this meeting, including editorial staff from Annals of Internal Medicine , BMJ , Bulletin of the World Health Organization , International Journal of Epidemiology , JAMA , Preventive Medicine , and The Lancet, as well as epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, and practitioners from Europe and North America.

span.label: Much biomedical research is observational and often inadequately reported, hampering assessment of strengths, weaknesses, and generalisability; STROBE offers a 22-item checklist for accurate, complete reporting.
span.quote: The reporting of such research is often inadequate, which hampers the assessment of its strengths and weaknesses and of a study's generalisability

span.label: Research should be reported transparently so readers can follow what was planned, done, found, and concluded.
span.quote: Research should be reported transparently so that readers can follow what was planned, what was done, what was found, and what conclusions were drawn

span.label: The checklist is 22 items: 18 common to all three designs, four design-specific.
span.quote: 18 items are common to all three study designs and four are specific for cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional studies.

span.label: The problem is documented, not assumed: 35% of longitudinal stroke studies did not state their eligibility criteria.
span.quote: In a survey of longitudinal studies in stroke research, 17 of 49 articles (35%) did not specify the eligibility criteria [ 8 ].

span.label: Choice of confounders often goes unreported, so a reader cannot tell what was adjusted for or why.
span.quote: An analysis of epidemiological studies published in general medical and specialist journals found that the rationale behind the choice of potential confounding variables was often not reported [ 6 ].

span.label: Case-control studies in psychiatry frequently omit how cases and controls were identified - the step the whole design rests on.
span.quote: Only few reports of case-control studies in psychiatry explained the methods used to identify cases and controls [ 7 ].

span.label: STROBE checklist (22 items)
span.quote: a checklist of 22 items (the STROBE Statement) that relate to the title, abstract, introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections

span.label: observational study designs
span.quote: three main study designs: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies

span.label: the STROBE Statement
span.quote: The STROBE Statement is a checklist of 22 items that we consider essential for good reporting of observational studies

span.label: transparent reporting
span.quote: Research should be reported transparently so that readers can follow what was planned, what was done, what was found, and what conclusions were drawn.

span.label: the scope of the recommendations
span.quote: We defined the scope of the recommendations to cover three main study designs: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies.
